Individuals shouldn't have a running tally of how many points they have. Instead, they should have a reputation, like Imgur or other forums do. This'll prevent point grabbing submissions and comments. Of course, you could still use a point system, just brand it a little differently. I'll illustrate using this table

IKP 0-100 100-200 300-400 500-600 600-700 800-900 1000 and up  
Rep Newbie Noticed Respected Well Rounded Well Known Popular Famous  

Of course, these are only examples. If you don't want to get rid of IKP, then perhaps you could make it so that it isn't public, and only the owner of the account can see it. Then you could have Rep AND IKP.

Another idea with reputation/IKP. It doesn't necessarily reflect the users actual helpfulness or anything, just how well their posts do. Maybe you could make it so that people can give badges, like on DeviantArt. If someone is extraordinarily helpful, go to their profile and give them a "Helpful" badge, and so on. If someone has 500 "Helpful" badges, then we know that that person is helpful, and it will reflect them much better than a point system.
Remove IKP/Contribution points, use a reputation-based score system instead.

I like the dA badges idea. Just nothing pointless like llamas...

Also, badges has the problem with being one-per-user, and people trading badges for badges, so perhaps make badges per-submission or per-post.
Making badges per-submission would essentially remove the point of upvoats. Upvoats are for judging posts, badges are for representing a user's attitude/personality.

Still, a user who posts a few good things spread out over time versus a user who posts lots of good but not as good things in a short timespan for a while will usually have their badges in the same general range I feel like.

Well, we could always copy Imgur's system. Have an ikp number, and then certain "point goals" that go along with it. The goals don't really offer anything significant, but having the word "Glorious" pinned up on your profile is a pretty nice feeling. Something like that could work for Voat, I think.
